name: Ayautla Mazatec
confidence_why: One first-hand description, checked against the source; 1 further work by the same author (or citing it for stress) agrees.

audit.action: a better source should be cited for the same classification
audit.reasoning: The classification (fixed-dominant, final syllable of the phonological word) rests on the only full phonological description of this variety, a 2020 UNAM MA thesis of xxv+389 pp classified by Glottolog as a phonology, and the quotation is verbatim at §3.3 p.107 and §6.2.1.1 p.221 of the PDF downloaded now. The author's 2024 open-access LangSci chapter independently restates obligatory, culminative, right-edge stress on the root+suffix domain with enclitics excluded, so nothing suggests a reclassify; the record previously held no file and carries an empty grade/cite/loc, so the action is to attach the now-held PDF (cite + locator p.107/p.221) and set the strength of the evidence. One nuance worth carrying into the domain field if it is ever coded: the stress domain is the phonological word (root + comitative suffix, compounds = last stem); syllabic enclitics are unstressed and outside it, and the description is i

sources.citation: Nakamoto 2020, Tonologia mazateca: San Bartolome Ayautla, MA thesis UNAM, hdl 20.500.14330/TES01000801819, full PDF secs. 3.3 and 6.2.1.1
sources.quote: El mazateco tiene acento fijo en la última sílaba de la palabra fonológica ... Incluso en los préstamos, el acento siempre cae en la sílaba final (§4.4.4). ... los prefijos silábicos no afectan la posición del acento.

sources.citation: Nakamoto, Shun. 2020. Tonología mazateca: San Bartolomé Ayautla. Tesis de maestría, Universidad Nacional Autónoma de México. hdl:20.500.14330/TES01000801819
sources.quote: 'El mazateco tiene acento fijo en la última sílaba de la palabra fonológica' (p.107); loans and prefixed forms keep final stress, comitative suffix -ko13 takes the stress, compounds stress the last stem, syllabic enclitics never stressed (pp.220-222); no secondary stress.
sources.venue: Tesis de maestría, Universidad Nacional Autónoma de México. hdl:20.500.14330/TES01000801819

sources.citation: Nakamoto, Shun. 2024. Constituency in Ayautla Mazatec. In Adam J.R. Tallman, Sandra Auderset & Hiroto Uchihara (eds.), Constituency and convergence in the Americas (Topics in Phonological Diversity 1), 231-264. Berlin: Language Science Press. DOI 10.5281/zenodo.10559861 (book); chapter PDF compiled from github.com/langsci/291 (Zenodo chapter record 13208548 timed out).
sources.quote: 'Stress in Ayautla Mazatec is phonetically semi-long with an increased intensity, and is obligatory, culminative and predictably assigned on the right edge (or the end) of the stress domain' -- domain = verb root plus comitative suffix (positions 19-20); enclitics after position 20 do not shift the stress; independent pronouns carry their own stress.
sources.locator: §3.8 'Stress assignment (19-20, 15-20)', chapter-pp. xx-xxi (PDF pages 20-21; published pagination ~250-251)
sources.venue: Constituency and convergence in the Americas (Topics in Phonological Diversity 1)

sources.quote: Lengua mazateca: [...] Características generales: - Acento fijo: sílaba final - Sílaba abierta [...] Datos: - Ayautla: notas de campo (19 días, 11/2017-3/2018) || Ayautla. Resumen: - Tonos léxicos: 1, 2, 3(4), 4, 12, 13, 23, 24, 34(, 3) - Sandhi: 3(4) - Repartimiento: 13 (compuesto), 23 - Propagación: 34, 13 (enclítico) || Notación tonal: "4" superíndice indica el tono más alto y "1" el más bajo.
sources.locator: §1.2 'La lengua y los datos', p. 3; §2 'Ayautla' Resumen, p. 3; fn. 2, p. 1; sandhi/repartimiento/propagación summaries pp. 4-5
sources.note: Oral presentation in Spanish at COLOV VIII (21 Apr 2018) on tone sandhi in Ayautla, Chiquihuitlán and Soyaltepec Mazatec and their correspondences; no written version located; the Ayautla sandhi facts are published in the known 2020 thesis (ch.5) and summarised in the Tlalocan 2020 introduction p.119 (tones 13 and 3 trigger tone 4 on the following morpheme).

sources.citation: 中本舜 [Nakamoto, Shun]. 2021. 「曲声調」とは何か：マサテク語アヤウトラ方言の曲声調から [What is a contour tone? From Ayautla Mazatec contour tones]. 『日本言語学会第163回大会予稿集』 (Proceedings of the 163rd Meeting of the Linguistic Society of Japan, online, 20-21 Nov 2021), paper B-4, pp. 73-79 [end page inferred from TOC: next paper starts p. 80]. 日本言語学会.
sources.note: Only/record: a paper on the status of contour tones in Ayautla Mazatec - whether its contour tones are unitary or sequences of level primitives (the thesis §4.1.2.3 argues /23/ and /3/-type contours include 'true contour tones'); likely restates the Ayautla tone-primitive inventory and tonotactics from Nakamoto 2020 with new argumentation; in Japanese.

sources.citation: Nakamoto, Shun & Josefina Sánchez Díaz. 2020. Na’ain Cho’on / El señor del trueno: un texto en mazateco de Ayautla. Tlalocan 25: 115-145. México: Instituto de Investigaciones Filológicas, UNAM. DOI 10.19130/iifl.tlalocan.2020.501 (Glottolog lists it as Sánchez Díaz & Nakamoto 2020).
sources.note: Glossed and analysed Ayautla Mazatec text with 'una introducción sobre algunos aspectos del mazateco de Ayautla' and morphological analysis - by the author of the Ayautla tonology, so the introduction very likely gives the tone notation (superscript digits) and a summary of the tone inventory/sandhi used in the transcription; first tone-notated published text of the variety.
